metadata.title: Six Agent Variants: How to Measure What Prompt Changes Actually Do
metadata.purpose: Answer one real question in the Plain register: you keep editing a slide-writing agent's prompt and eyeballing the new deck against the old one — how do you actually know a change helped, and how do you tell a prompt win from a model win? Lands the carry-out that every version is scored against the same fixed test and the same pinned baseline, and that a rule living only in the prompt doesn't survive a model swap. Redo of the cwc-workshops Teardown workshop-teardown cut; facts re-grounded directly against the workshop repo (the source's six-step waterfall of invented percentages and agent techniques not in the repo is dropped).
metadata.anchor_pair: S03 -> S08 (must be the SAME case: the mandatory-diagram grader, present then empty)
metadata.one_flag: none needed - all claims restate the workshop repo's own files, not this reel's inference

beats.narration_text: A newcomer tweaks their agent's prompt, looks at the new deck, and calls it better. That's a glance, not a measurement. So what does actually testing a prompt change look like, round after round?

shot.new_visual_element: Writer types the naive claim, hesitates on 'looks', corrects to 'scores', lands the real question

props.text:
My new prompt looks better. Done.
But how do I know it's actually better?

beats.narration_text: You've got a Claude agent that writes slide decks, and you keep editing its system prompt hoping each version beats the last — for five different topics, every time.

shot.new_visual_element: A prompt, edited again, feeding the same five tasks

production_viz.label: A prompt, edited again, feeding the same five tasks
production_viz.mechanic: A system-prompt card on the left with a pencil-edit mark. An arrow fans out to five small task cards on the right (career, environment, food, social, tech), each producing a slide-deck icon.

beats.narration_text: The natural read: open the new deck, glance at it next to the old one, and if it looks cleaner, ship it — glance in, glance out, decision made.

shot.new_visual_element: Two decks, a glance, a decision

production_viz.label: Two decks, a glance, a decision
production_viz.mechanic: Two slide-deck icons side by side (OLD / NEW). An eye icon sweeps between them once, then a checkmark stamps 'SHIP IT' — sell the reading as reasonable and fast.

beats.narration_text: Hold onto one rule: every slide has to carry a real diagram, not just text and boxes — and one grader does nothing but count whether that actually happened.

shot.new_visual_element: THE ANCHOR — the diagram rule, and its counter

production_viz.label: THE ANCHOR — the diagram rule, and its counter
production_viz.mechanic: THE ANCHOR. A slide silhouette with a required image-slot outlined in teal. Beside it a tally counter reading '5 / 5 SLIDES'. THIS EXACT COMPOSITION RETURNS AT S08.

beats.narration_text: But a glance won't catch a nine-point caption sitting under the ten-point floor on slide four — a code grader parses the file's actual font sizes and catches it in milliseconds, no eyeballing required.

shot.new_visual_element: The glance misses it; the parser doesn't

production_viz.label: The glance misses it; the parser doesn't
production_viz.mechanic: The S02 eye icon sweeps past slide four and nods approval. Beneath it, the same slide zoomed in: a caption reading '9pt' flagged crimson against a '10pt FLOOR' line, caught by a code-bracket icon in milliseconds.

beats.narration_text: The eval runs in two layers. Layer one is code — parsing the deck file itself: slide count, images present, cluttered slides, tiny fonts, stray emoji. No model call, pass or fail in milliseconds.

shot.new_visual_element: Layer one: the code checks, ticking down

production_viz.label: Layer one: the code checks, ticking down
production_viz.mechanic: A .pptx file icon feeds into a code-bracket gear. Five check-cards tick down in teal: SLIDE COUNT, IMAGES PRESENT, CLUTTER, FONT SIZE, EMOJI. A small 'no model call' badge sits beside the gear.

beats.narration_text: Layer two hands the rendered slide images to an LLM judge, scoring text, imagery, layout, color, and whether the title actually matches the body underneath it.

shot.new_visual_element: Layer two: the rendered slide, judged

production_viz.label: Layer two: the rendered slide, judged
production_viz.mechanic: A rendered slide image feeds into a robed-judge icon (simple geometric gavel/eye mark, no likeness). Five scoring dials fill in: TEXT, IMAGE, LAYOUT, COLOR, TITLE-BODY.

beats.narration_text: Round one just tightens typography and trims word count. Round two adds that mandatory diagram. Round three adds a QA loop — the agent rasterizes its own deck, inspects every slide for overlap and overflow, fixes what it finds, and checks again before it's done.

shot.new_visual_element: Three rounds, each adding one rule

production_viz.label: Three rounds, each adding one rule
production_viz.mechanic: Three stacked round-cards building left to right: 'ROUND 1 · TYPOGRAPHY', 'ROUND 2 · DIAGRAM' (teal, ties to the anchor slot), 'ROUND 3 · QA LOOP' with a small self-inspect icon (magnifying glass over its own deck).

beats.narration_text: Then round four breaks the pattern entirely — it drops every one of those rules and goes back to the plain prompt, just on a stronger model. Check that same diagram grader, and it's empty again: that rule only ever lived in the prompt.

shot.new_visual_element: THE ANCHOR RETURNS — the diagram slot, empty

production_viz.label: THE ANCHOR RETURNS — the diagram slot, empty
production_viz.mechanic: THE S03 COMPOSITION RETURNS, identical. 'ROUND 4 · MODEL SWAP' card appears with the three prior round-cards crossed out. The tally counter that read '5 / 5 SLIDES' resets to '0 / 5 SLIDES' in crimson. A new-model badge appears beside a dimmed old-model badge.

beats.narration_text: When a code check fails — no diagram, a caption under the size floor — that's a concrete defect, proven the moment the file's parsed, no judgment call needed.

shot.new_visual_element: A code fail: proven, no judgment needed

production_viz.label: A code fail: proven, no judgment needed
production_viz.mechanic: A code-bracket icon stamps a crimson 'FAIL' on a parsed fact (missing image slot). Label beneath: 'PROVEN AT PARSE TIME.' No judge icon anywhere in frame.

beats.narration_text: But every code check passing doesn't mean the deck is good — a slide can hit every rule and still not explain the idea, which is exactly what the LLM judge is there to catch.

shot.new_visual_element: Mirroring S09: all code checks pass, judge still needed

production_viz.label: Mirroring S09: all code checks pass, judge still needed
production_viz.mechanic: Mirroring S09's layout: five code checks all tick teal 'PASS'. The slide sits there anyway, flat and unclear. The judge icon from S06 reappears and circles a low 'TITLE-BODY' dial in crimson.

beats.narration_text: Score every version against the same fixed test and the same pinned baseline — a rule that only lives in the prompt doesn't survive a model swap.

props.quote: Score every version against the same fixed test and the same pinned baseline — a rule that only lives in the prompt doesn't survive a model swap.

beats.narration_text: Your turn. Here's the prompt — read it with me: "Take an agent I'm iterating on. Freeze one fixed test set of real inputs, write one code check that's just a plain fact — present or not — and one rubric a judge model can score from the rendered result. Run every version, including one where I swap the model instead of the prompt, against that same test and the same pinned baseline. What actually moved, and what only looked like it moved?" Liam, in for Bear.
